papers.title: Online Data Selection for Instruction Tuning via Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: With Large Language Model (LLM) pre-training and fine-tuning shifting its focus from data volume to data quality, quality data selection has emerged as a critical research topic. Existing online data selection methods for LLM training are typically "batch-constrained", limiting optimization to local utility within random batches. To overcome this, we propose GAIA (Global Adaptive Instruction tuning via GAussian processes), a framework that formulates data valuation as a global estimation process. GAIA employs Gaussian Process regression to model continuous utility manifolds across the semantic space, utilizing an adaptive strategy fusion mechanism to dynamically prioritize high-utility samples. By casting the strategy-posterior update as an instance of the classical fixed-share Hedge framework for tracking the best expert, we inherit a dynamic-regret guarantee that characterizes GAIA's robustness under non-stationary quality scores during training. Empirical evaluations on three datasets demonstrate that GAIA significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines like \greats, establishing our method as a scalable and robust solution for efficient instruction tuning.

summary.takeaway: GAIA leverages Gaussian Process regression with a fixed-share Hedge update to globally and adaptively select high-utility instruction tuning data, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines like GREATS with minimal overhead.
summary.problem: Existing online data selection methods for LLM instruction tuning are batch-constrained, limiting optimization to local utility within randomly sampled candidate pools and thus suffering from stochastic vulnerability.
summary.method: GAIA models the latent quality function over the entire training corpus using Gaussian Processes, discretizes it into strategies, and updates their posterior via a fixed-share Hedge algorithm to guide global candidate pool construction and adaptive data selection.
summary.evidence: Empirical evaluations on three instruction tuning datasets and four backbone LLMs show GAIA-GREATS achieves faster convergence and better perplexity and accuracy than baselines, adding only about 23 seconds overhead on a 13k-sample dataset.
summary.limitations: The method requires warm-up initialization with a small labeled subset and tuning of Hedge learning and mixing rates, with no explicit mechanism detailed for handling extremely large-scale datasets beyond the tested scale.
summary.why_for_you: GAIA offers a theoretically grounded, scalable, and robust framework for improving data selection quality in LLM instruction tuning, directly addressing batch-constrained limitations relevant to efficient and trustworthy LLM training.

signals.text: GAIA employs Gaussian Process regression to model a continuous latent quality function over the entire training corpus, enabling principled generalization of data valuation signals to unseen examples throughout training.
The fixed-share Hedge update mechanism maintains a posterior over discretized GP strategies, allowing dynamic adaptation to non-stationary quality scores with a provable dynamic-regret guarantee.

Empirical results on MMLU, SAMSUM, and TYDIQA datasets with LLaMA-2, LLaMA-3, Qwen, and Mistral backbones show GAIA-GREATS significantly accelerates convergence and improves test perplexity and accuracy compared to GREATS and other baselines.

deep_dive.overview: The paper addresses the critical challenge of online data selection for instruction tuning of LLMs, where existing methods are limited by batch-constrained candidate pools sampled uniformly at random, causing local optimality and stochastic vulnerability. GAIA proposes a global data valuation framework by modeling the latent quality function over the entire training corpus using Gaussian Processes, enabling smooth generalization of utility scores to unseen data. To scale this approach, GAIA discretizes the GP into a finite set of strategies and maintains a posterior distribution over them via a fixed-share Hedge update, which adapts to the non-stationarity of quality scores as model parameters evolve. This posterior guides the sampling of candidate batches biased toward high-utility regions, which can be further refined by existing selection methods like GREATS. Empirical evaluations on multiple datasets and LLM architectures demonstrate that GAIA significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines with negligible computational overhead, validating its effectiveness and scalability as a robust online data selection method for instruction tuning.

methodology.title: Gaussian Process Modeling
methodology.detail: GAIA models the latent quality function over the entire training corpus as a Gaussian Process (GP) with a kernel fitted on warm-up data. This enables continuous estimation of data utility across the semantic embedding space, allowing generalization to unseen samples.

methodology.title: Strategy Discretization and Posterior Maintenance
methodology.detail: The continuous GP is discretized into a finite set of function samples called strategies. GAIA maintains a posterior distribution over these strategies using a fixed-share Hedge update with a top-k likelihood, allowing adaptation to changing data quality during training.

methodology.title: Fixed-Share Hedge Update
methodology.detail: To handle non-stationary quality scores, GAIA uses a fixed-share Hedge update that mixes the posterior with a uniform distribution at each step, preventing permanent exclusion of any strategy and providing a dynamic-regret guarantee for robustness.

methodology.title: Candidate Batch Sampling
methodology.detail: At each iteration, GAIA samples a strategy from the posterior and draws candidate batches from the training pool with probabilities proportional to the exponentiated strategy scores, controlled by a temperature parameter to balance exploitation and diversity.

methodology.title: Integration with Existing Selection Methods
methodology.detail: GAIA can be combined with methods like GREATS by first globally biasing candidate pool sampling toward high-utility regions, then applying local batch refinement to optimize quality and diversity within the batch.

mechanism.title: Dynamic Posterior Update via Fixed-Share Hedge
mechanism.detail: GAIA models the posterior over strategies with a fixed-share Hedge update that tempers each batch's evidence by a learning rate λ and mixes with a uniform distribution at rate α. This update admits a Bayesian interpretation as filtering under a Markovian switching prior, enabling recovery from shifts in the best strategy as model parameters evolve.

experiments.title: Datasets and Models
experiments.detail: Evaluations were conducted on three instruction tuning datasets: MMLU, SAMSUM, and TYDIQA, using four backbone LLMs: LLaMA-2-7B, LLaMA-3-18B, Qwen-3.4B, and Mistral-7B.

experiments.title: Baselines and Metrics
experiments.detail: GAIA was compared against gradient-based (GradNorm), loss-prioritizing (MaxLoss, RHOLoss), semantic-aware (SBERT), and greedy optimization (GREATS) baselines, using perplexity and accuracy metrics on validation and test sets.

experiments.title: Efficiency and Overhead
experiments.detail: GAIA adds minimal computational overhead, e.g., approximately 23 seconds for GP training on a 13k-sample MMLU dataset, demonstrating practical scalability.

experiments.title: Ablations and Sensitivity
experiments.detail: The effect of sampling temperature τ and embedding dimensionality via SVD projection were analyzed, showing a trade-off between exploitation speed and batch diversity.

findings.title: Improved Convergence
findings.detail: GAIA-GREATS achieves significantly faster convergence in perplexity and accuracy on MMLU-Sociology and SAMSUM compared to all baselines, demonstrating the benefit of global adaptive data selection.

findings.title: Robustness to Non-Stationarity
findings.detail: The fixed-share Hedge update enables GAIA to adapt to evolving data quality during training, maintaining a dynamic-regret guarantee and preventing strategy collapse.

findings.title: Minimal Overhead
findings.detail: Despite the added complexity of GP modeling and posterior updates, GAIA incurs negligible runtime overhead relative to baseline training times.

findings.title: Effective Integration
findings.detail: Combining GAIA with GREATS leverages global guidance and local batch refinement, yielding superior performance over either method alone.

contributions: Formulation of data valuation as a global estimation problem using Gaussian Processes over the entire training corpus.
Introduction of a fixed-share Hedge posterior update to handle non-stationary quality scores with dynamic-regret guarantees.
A scalable and computationally efficient framework that integrates with existing online data selection methods to improve instruction tuning.
Comprehensive empirical validation on multiple datasets and LLM architectures demonstrating superior performance and efficiency.
limitations: Requires a warm-up phase with labeled data to fit the initial GP model, which may limit applicability in fully unsupervised settings.
Hyperparameters of the fixed-share Hedge update (learning rate λ and mixing rate α) require empirical tuning without automated adaptation.
Scalability beyond the tested dataset sizes and embedding dimensions is not explicitly demonstrated.
No explicit mechanism is provided for handling extremely large or streaming datasets beyond the discretized strategy approach.
open_questions: How can GAIA be extended or adapted to fully unsupervised or zero-label scenarios without warm-up initialization?
Can the fixed-share Hedge update parameters be learned or adapted online to reduce hyperparameter tuning?
What are the limits of GAIA's scalability in terms of dataset size, embedding dimensionality, and model scale?
How does GAIA perform in continual learning or streaming data scenarios where data distribution shifts significantly?

signals.text: GAIA采用高斯过程回归（Gaussian Process regression）对整个训练语料库上的连续潜在质量函数进行建模，实现了数据估值信号对训练过程中未见样本的原则性泛化。
固定份额Hedge更新机制（fixed-share Hedge update）维护离散化高斯过程策略的后验分布，允许动态适应非平稳的质量评分，并具备可证明的动态遗憾保证。
在MMLU、SAMSUM和TYDIQA数据集上，结合LLaMA-2、LLaMA-3、Qwen和Mistral骨干模型的实证结果表明，GAIA-GREATS相比GREATS及其他基线显著加速收敛并提升测试困惑度（perplexity）和准确率（accuracy）。

zh-CN.overview: 本文针对大规模语言模型（LLMs）指令微调中的在线数据选择这一关键挑战，指出现有方法受限于批次约束的候选池且均匀随机采样，导致局部最优和随机脆弱性。GAIA提出了基于高斯过程（Gaussian Processes）对整个训练语料库潜在质量函数进行建模的全局数据估值框架，实现了效用分数对未见数据的平滑泛化。为扩展该方法，GAIA将高斯过程离散化为有限策略集，并通过固定份额Hedge更新维护其后验分布，适应模型参数演化导致的质量分数非平稳性。该后验引导候选批次采样，偏向高效用区域，且可结合GREATS等现有选择方法进一步优化。多数据集和多模型架构的实证评估表明，GAIA在计算开销极小的情况下显著优于最先进基线，验证了其作为稳健在线数据选择方法在指令微调中的有效性和可扩展性。

methodology.title: 高斯过程建模（Gaussian Process Modeling）
methodology.detail: GAIA将整个训练语料库上的潜在质量函数建模为高斯过程（GP），其核函数基于预热数据拟合，实现了语义嵌入空间中数据效用的连续估计，支持对未见样本的泛化。

methodology.title: 策略离散化与后验维护（Strategy Discretization and Posterior Maintenance）
methodology.detail: 将连续的高斯过程离散为有限函数样本集，称为策略。GAIA通过固定份额Hedge更新结合top-k似然维护这些策略的后验分布，适应训练过程中数据质量的变化。

methodology.title: 固定份额Hedge更新（Fixed-Share Hedge Update）
methodology.detail: 为应对非平稳质量分数，GAIA采用固定份额Hedge更新，在每步将后验与均匀分布混合，防止任何策略被永久排除，并提供动态遗憾保证以增强鲁棒性。

methodology.title: 候选批次采样（Candidate Batch Sampling）
methodology.detail: 每次迭代中，GAIA从后验中采样策略，并根据策略分数的指数加权概率从训练池中抽取候选批次，温度参数控制利用与多样性的平衡。

methodology.title: 与现有选择方法的集成（Integration with Existing Selection Methods）
methodology.detail: GAIA可与GREATS等方法结合，先全局偏向高效用区域采样候选池，再局部批次优化以提升批次内质量和多样性。

mechanism.title: 通过固定份额Hedge的动态后验更新（Dynamic Posterior Update via Fixed-Share Hedge）
mechanism.detail: GAIA利用固定份额Hedge更新对策略后验建模，该更新以学习率λ调节每批次证据，并以混合率α与均匀分布混合。此更新可视为带马尔可夫切换先验的贝叶斯滤波，支持模型参数演化时最佳策略的恢复。

experiments.title: 数据集与模型（Datasets and Models）
experiments.detail: 评估涵盖三个指令微调数据集：MMLU、SAMSUM和TYDIQA，使用四个骨干大语言模型：LLaMA-2-7B、LLaMA-3-18B、Qwen-3.4B和Mistral-7B。

experiments.title: 基线与指标（Baselines and Metrics）
experiments.detail: GAIA与基于梯度的GradNorm、优先损失的MaxLoss和RHOLoss、语义感知的SBERT及贪心优化的GREATS基线比较，采用验证集和测试集上的困惑度和准确率指标。

experiments.title: 效率与开销（Efficiency and Overhead）
experiments.detail: GAIA计算开销极小，例如在13k样本的MMLU数据集上高斯过程训练约需23秒，展示了实用的可扩展性。

experiments.title: 消融与敏感性分析（Ablations and Sensitivity）
experiments.detail: 分析了采样温度τ和通过奇异值分解（SVD）投影的嵌入维度对性能的影响，揭示了利用速度与批次多样性之间的权衡。

findings.title: 收敛性提升（Improved Convergence）
findings.detail: GAIA-GREATS在MMLU-社会学和SAMSUM数据集上，在困惑度和准确率方面显著快于所有基线，体现了全局自适应数据选择的优势。

findings.title: 对非平稳性的鲁棒性（Robustness to Non-Stationarity）
findings.detail: 固定份额Hedge更新使GAIA能适应训练中数据质量的演变，维持动态遗憾保证，防止策略崩溃。

findings.title: 极小的开销（Minimal Overhead）
findings.detail: 尽管引入了高斯过程建模和后验更新，GAIA相较基线训练时间几乎无额外运行时开销。

findings.title: 有效的集成（Effective Integration）
findings.detail: GAIA与GREATS结合利用全局引导和局部批次优化，性能优于单独使用任一方法。

contributions: 将数据估值问题形式化为基于整个训练语料库的高斯过程全局估计问题。
引入固定份额Hedge后验更新以处理非平稳质量分数，具备动态遗憾保证。
提出可扩展且计算高效的框架，能与现有在线数据选择方法集成以提升指令微调效果。
在多数据集和多大语言模型架构上进行全面实证验证，展示优越的性能和效率。
limitations: 需要带标签数据的预热阶段以拟合初始高斯过程模型，限制了在完全无监督场景下的适用性。
固定份额Hedge更新的超参数（学习率λ和混合率α）需经验调优，缺乏自动适应机制。
未明确展示在更大数据集规模和更高嵌入维度下的可扩展性。
未提供针对极大规模或流式数据集的显式处理机制，除离散策略方法外。
open_questions: 如何扩展或适配GAIA以支持无预热初始化的完全无监督或零标签场景？
固定份额Hedge更新参数能否在线学习或自适应以减少超参数调优？
GAIA在数据集规模、嵌入维度和模型规模方面的可扩展性极限为何？
在数据分布显著变化的持续学习或流式数据场景中，GAIA表现如何？

papers.title: Labeling Training Data for Entity Matching Using Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Recent large language models (LLMs) achieve strong performance on entity matching without requiring task-specific training data. However, applying these models to large sets of candidate pairs remains slow and costly. In contrast, entity matchers using traditional machine learning methods or small language models (SLMs), such as RoBERTa, offer much faster inference but require task-specific training data. This paper investigates whether the need to provide task-specific training data can be avoided by using knowledge-distillation workflows, in which an LLM serves as a teacher model to label training pairs that are subsequently used to train a smaller student model. We investigate knowledge distillation for entity matching along the following dimensions: pair-selection strategy, teacher model, label post-processing method, and student model. We evaluate the workflows using the Abt-Buy, Walmart-Amazon, WDC Products, DBLP-ACM, and DBLP-Scholar benchmarks, and compare the performance of student models trained with machine-labeled data to the performance of the same models trained using the benchmark training sets. Our experiments show that student models trained using the machine-labeled sets perform approximately on par with models trained on the benchmark training sets, with the remaining differences in both directions staying below two F1 points. Using GPT-5.2 to label the training sets for all five benchmarks costs US\$28.31 to US\$40.88, whereas manually labeling the same training sets is estimated to require 470 hours of work. At inference time, Ditto is 41.5 to 534 times faster than directly using an LLM to perform the matching tasks. These results indicate that current LLMs, when combined with a suitable pair-selection method, can substantially reduce or even eliminate the manual effort required to label use case-specific training data for entity matching.

summary.takeaway: Recent large language models (LLMs) achieve strong performance on entity matching without requiring task-specific training data.
summary.problem: Recent large language models (LLMs) achieve strong performance on entity matching without requiring task-specific training data.

papers.title: KbSD: Knowledge Boundary aware Self-Distillation for Behavioral Calibration in Agentic Search
papers.abstract: Agentic search equips large language models with dynamic retrieval abilities, but existing reinforcement learning methods remain limited by reward sparsity in knowledge boundary calibration -- deciding when to trust parametric memory, when to rely on retrieved evidence, and when to abstain. Binary rewards can penalize undesirable outcomes, but provide little guidance on the reasoning process required to make calibrated decisions across different knowledge states. To address this, we propose KbSD (Knowledge boundary Self-Distillation), a framework that tackles this limitation through dense token-level supervision, outcome-level sparse rewards, and quadrant-adaptive optimization. KbSD constructs a hint-augmented teacher, architecturally identical to the student, that receives explicit knowledge boundary signals -- including parametric certainty, retrieval quality, and ground-truth answers -- to generate calibrated reasoning demonstrations. This information-asymmetric self-distillation enables dense supervision without requiring a larger external model. To further account for the heterogeneous reasoning distributions across knowledge states, we introduce a quadrant-adaptive distillation objective: reverse KL for concentrated integration, forward KL for diverse refusal, and Pareto-optimal bidirectional KL for asymmetric quadrants requiring both precision and coverage. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show that KbSD consistently improves both task accuracy and hallucination mitigation over strong baselines, with the largest gains appearing in the challenging quadrants where sparse rewards are least informative.

summary.takeaway: KbSD introduces a quadrant-adaptive self-distillation framework that provides dense token-level supervision and tailored KL divergence objectives to improve knowledge boundary calibration in agentic search.
summary.problem: Existing reinforcement learning methods for agentic search suffer from sparse binary rewards that inadequately guide the reasoning process for calibrated decisions across heterogeneous knowledge states.
summary.method: KbSD constructs a hint-augmented teacher model identical to the student that receives explicit knowledge boundary signals to generate dense reasoning demonstrations and applies quadrant-adaptive KL objectives for optimized distillation.
summary.evidence: Experiments on nine benchmarks with Qwen2.5 models show KbSD consistently reduces unreliability rates and improves task accuracy and hallucination mitigation compared to strong baselines including KbPO and RL-based agents.
summary.limitations: The paper does not provide explicit analysis on the computational overhead of the self-distillation process or its applicability to models beyond Qwen2.5 and the tested datasets.
summary.why_for_you: KbSD’s approach to dense process-level supervision and quadrant-specific optimization directly addresses reward sparsity and heterogeneous reasoning distributions, advancing trustworthy on-policy distillation in agentic LLMs.

signals.text: KbSD’s quadrant-adaptive distillation uses reverse KL for concentrated integration (Q1), forward KL for diverse refusal (Q3), and bidirectional KL for asymmetric quadrants (Q2/Q4), effectively tailoring optimization to heterogeneous reasoning distributions.

The hint-augmented teacher model receives parametric certainty, retrieval quality, and ground-truth answers as explicit knowledge boundary signals, enabling dense token-level supervision without requiring a larger external teacher.

Ablation studies show removing distillation loss or replacing quadrant-adaptive KL with fixed KL variants degrades performance, confirming the necessity of dense supervision and adaptive divergence objectives for reliable calibration.

deep_dive.overview: Agentic search in LLMs requires calibrated decisions on when to trust parametric memory, rely on retrieved evidence, or abstain, but sparse binary rewards provide insufficient guidance for this complex reasoning. KbSD addresses this by introducing a self-distillation framework that leverages a hint-augmented teacher model to generate dense token-level supervision informed by explicit knowledge boundary signals. This dense supervision guides the student model through the full cognitive process of assessing internal certainty and retrieval quality. To handle the heterogeneous reasoning patterns across four knowledge boundary quadrants, KbSD employs quadrant-adaptive KL divergence objectives: reverse KL for unimodal integration, forward KL for diverse refusal, and bidirectional KL for asymmetric cases requiring both precision and coverage. Empirical results on nine diverse benchmarks with Qwen2.5 models demonstrate that KbSD consistently lowers unreliability rates and improves task accuracy and hallucination mitigation compared to strong baselines, with the largest gains in challenging quadrants where sparse rewards are least informative. Ablations validate the critical role of dense supervision and adaptive KL objectives, establishing KbSD as a robust method for behavioral calibration in agentic search.

methodology.title: Hint-Augmented Teacher Construction
methodology.detail: KbSD builds a teacher model architecturally identical to the student that receives explicit knowledge boundary signals—parametric certainty, retrieval quality, and ground-truth answers—to produce calibrated reasoning demonstrations. This information asymmetry enables dense token-level supervision without requiring a larger external teacher model.

methodology.title: Quadrant-Adaptive Distillation Objective
methodology.detail: The distillation loss adapts the KL divergence measure per knowledge quadrant: reverse KL for concentrated, unimodal integration in Q1; forward KL for diverse refusal behavior in Q3; and Pareto-optimal bidirectional KL for asymmetric quadrants Q2 and Q4 that require balancing precision and coverage.

methodology.title: Dense Token-Level Supervision
methodology.detail: Beyond sparse outcome-level rewards, KbSD provides dense supervision at each reasoning step, guiding the agent through intermediate cognitive processes such as assessing internal certainty and retrieval relevance, thus addressing reward sparsity and enabling fine-grained behavioral calibration.

methodology.title: Training Setup and Optimization
methodology.detail: KbSD is implemented on the VERL framework with GRPO optimizer, training Qwen2.5 models (3B and 7B) on synthesized data from HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA. Training uses batch size 128, 5 rollouts per query, learning rate 1e-6, and balances distillation and process rewards with coefficients γ=0.1 and λ=0.2.

mechanism.title: Knowledge Boundary Quadrants
mechanism.detail: KbSD formalizes knowledge boundary calibration into four quadrants defined by internal knowledge reliability and retrieval quality: Q1 (both reliable, integrate), Q2 (rely on retrieval), Q3 (refuse to answer), and Q4 (rely on internal knowledge). Each quadrant exhibits distinct reasoning distribution characteristics requiring tailored optimization.

mechanism.title: No Explicit Mechanistic Equations
mechanism.detail: The paper does not provide explicit mathematical equations or causal models beyond the quadrant taxonomy and KL divergence adaptations; the mechanism relies on empirical adaptation of divergence objectives to heterogeneous reasoning distributions.

experiments.title: Benchmark Evaluation
experiments.detail: KbSD is evaluated on nine benchmarks spanning multi-hop QA (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, Bamboogle), open-domain QA (NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA), and agentic reasoning (FRAMES, GAIA), using Qwen2.5 models at 3B and 7B scales with E5 dense retriever over 2018 Wikipedia.

experiments.title: Baselines and Metrics
experiments.detail: Comparisons include standard RAG methods (Naive RAG, FS-RAG, FLARE), agentic RAG (ReAct, IRCoT, Self-RAG, CRAG), and RL-based agents (Search-R1, ARPO, AEPO, MEM1, KbPO). Metrics are F1 for task utility and unreliability rate (1 - (F1 + refusal rate)) for unsafe behaviors.

experiments.title: Ablation Studies
experiments.detail: Ablations on Qwen2.5-3B show removing distillation loss or replacing quadrant-adaptive KL with fixed forward or reverse KL degrades performance, especially on benchmarks requiring diverse refusal or concentrated integration, confirming the importance of each design component.

findings.title: Improved Reliability Across Scales
findings.detail: KbSD reduces unreliability rates from 64.32 to 47.60 on Qwen2.5-3B and from 57.99 to 41.18 on Qwen2.5-7B, demonstrating consistent reliability gains that scale with model size.

findings.title: Superior Knowledge Boundary Calibration
findings.detail: KbSD outperforms Search-R1 and AEPO on TriviaQA and NQ benchmarks, showing substantial improvements in precise calibration of when to integrate, rely on retrieval, or refuse, especially in challenging quadrants with sparse rewards.

findings.title: Necessity of Dense Supervision
findings.detail: Removing the distillation loss causes performance degradation across all benchmarks, indicating that dense token-level supervision is essential to overcome reward sparsity and guide intermediate reasoning.

findings.title: Effectiveness of Quadrant-Adaptive KL
findings.detail: Replacing quadrant-adaptive KL with fixed forward or reverse KL harms performance, particularly on TriviaQA (diverse refusal) and 2WikiMultiHopQA (concentrated integration), validating the need for adaptive divergence objectives.

contributions: Proposed KbSD, a self-distillation framework that leverages a hint-augmented teacher to provide dense token-level supervision for knowledge boundary calibration.
Introduced a quadrant-adaptive KL divergence objective tailored to heterogeneous reasoning distributions across four knowledge boundary quadrants.
Demonstrated consistent improvements in task accuracy and hallucination mitigation over strong baselines on nine diverse benchmarks.
Provided ablation studies validating the necessity of dense supervision and quadrant-adaptive optimization.
Released code to facilitate reproducibility and further research.
limitations: Lack of explicit analysis on computational cost and efficiency of the self-distillation process.
Evaluation limited to Qwen2.5 models and selected QA and agentic reasoning benchmarks, leaving generalization to other architectures and tasks untested.
No detailed exploration of failure modes or qualitative analysis of reasoning trajectories.
Absence of explicit mechanistic or causal modeling beyond empirical KL divergence adaptations.
open_questions: How does KbSD scale computationally and perform on larger or different LLM architectures beyond Qwen2.5?
Can the quadrant-adaptive distillation framework be extended to other agentic tasks beyond QA and retrieval-augmented generation?
What are the qualitative characteristics of the reasoning trajectories learned under dense supervision, and how do they differ across quadrants?
How robust is KbSD to noisy or adversarial retrieval evidence in real-world deployment scenarios?

signals.text: KbSD 的象限自适应蒸馏使用反向 KL（reverse KL）进行集中整合（Q1），正向 KL（forward KL）进行多样拒绝（Q3），以及双向 KL（bidirectional KL）处理不对称象限（Q2/Q4），有效地针对异质推理分布定制优化。
提示增强的教师模型接收参数确定性、检索质量和真实答案作为显式知识边界信号，实现密集的令牌级监督，无需更大的外部教师模型。
消融研究表明，移除蒸馏损失或用固定 KL 变体替代象限自适应 KL 会降低性能，确认了密集监督和自适应散度目标对于可靠校准的必要性。

zh-CN.overview: 大型语言模型（LLMs）中的自主搜索需要对何时信任参数记忆、依赖检索证据或选择放弃做出校准决策，但稀疏的二元奖励无法为这一复杂推理提供充分指导。KbSD 通过引入一个利用提示增强教师模型生成基于显式知识边界信号的密集令牌级监督的自蒸馏框架来解决此问题。该密集监督引导学生模型完成评估内部确定性和检索质量的完整认知过程。为处理四个知识边界象限中异质的推理模式，KbSD 采用象限自适应 KL 散度目标：反向 KL 用于单峰整合，正向 KL 用于多样拒绝，双向 KL 用于需要兼顾精度和覆盖率的不对称象限。基于 Qwen2.5 模型在九个多样化基准上的实证结果表明，KbSD 持续降低不可靠率并提升任务准确率及幻觉缓解效果，相较强基线在奖励最稀疏的挑战性象限中获得最大提升。消融验证了密集监督和自适应 KL 目标的关键作用，确立了 KbSD 作为自主搜索行为校准的稳健方法。

methodology.title: 提示增强教师构建
methodology.detail: KbSD 构建了一个与学生模型结构相同的教师模型，接收显式知识边界信号——参数确定性、检索质量和真实答案，以生成校准的推理示范。这种信息不对称实现了密集的令牌级监督，无需更大的外部教师模型。

methodology.title: 象限自适应蒸馏目标
methodology.detail: 蒸馏损失根据知识象限调整 KL 散度度量：Q1 中用于集中单峰整合的反向 KL；Q3 中用于多样拒绝行为的正向 KL；以及 Q2 和 Q4 中需平衡精度与覆盖率的不对称象限采用帕累托最优的双向 KL。

methodology.title: 密集令牌级监督
methodology.detail: 除了稀疏的结果级奖励外，KbSD 在每个推理步骤提供密集监督，引导代理完成评估内部确定性和检索相关性等中间认知过程，从而解决奖励稀疏问题并实现细粒度行为校准。

methodology.title: 训练设置与优化
methodology.detail: KbSD 基于 VERL 框架实现，采用 GRPO 优化器，训练 Qwen2.5 模型（3B 和 7B）使用 HotpotQA 和 2WikiMultiHopQA 合成数据。训练批量大小为 128，每个查询 5 次 rollout，学习率 1e-6，蒸馏与过程奖励权重系数分别为 γ=0.1 和 λ=0.2。

mechanism.title: 知识边界象限
mechanism.detail: KbSD 将知识边界校准形式化为由内部知识可靠性和检索质量定义的四个象限：Q1（两者均可靠，整合），Q2（依赖检索），Q3（拒绝回答），Q4（依赖内部知识）。每个象限表现出不同的推理分布特征，需定制优化。

mechanism.title: 无显式机制方程
mechanism.detail: 论文未提供除象限分类和 KL 散度调整外的显式数学方程或因果模型；机制依赖于对异质推理分布的散度目标的经验性调整。

experiments.title: 基准评估
experiments.detail: KbSD 在九个基准上评估，涵盖多跳问答（HotpotQA、2WikiMultiHopQA、MuSiQue、Bamboogle）、开放域问答（NQ、TriviaQA、PopQA）和自主推理（FRAMES、GAIA），使用 Qwen2.5 3B 和 7B 模型，配合基于 2018 年维基百科的 E5 密集检索器。

experiments.title: 基线与指标
experiments.detail: 比较方法包括标准 RAG（Naive RAG、FS-RAG、FLARE）、自主 RAG（ReAct、IRCoT、Self-RAG、CRAG）和基于强化学习的代理（Search-R1、ARPO、AEPO、MEM1、KbPO）。指标为任务效用的 F1 和不安全行为的不可依赖率（1 - (F1 + 拒绝率)）。

experiments.title: 消融研究
experiments.detail: 在 Qwen2.5-3B 上的消融显示，移除蒸馏损失或用固定正向或反向 KL 替代象限自适应 KL 会降低性能，尤其在需要多样拒绝或集中整合的基准上，验证了各设计组件的重要性。

findings.title: 跨规模提升可靠性
findings.detail: KbSD 将 Qwen2.5-3B 的不可依赖率从 64.32 降至 47.60，Qwen2.5-7B 从 57.99 降至 41.18，展示了随模型规模增长的一致可靠性提升。

findings.title: 卓越的知识边界校准
findings.detail: KbSD 在 TriviaQA 和 NQ 基准上优于 Search-R1 和 AEPO，显著提升了何时整合、依赖检索或拒绝的精确校准，尤其在奖励稀疏的挑战性象限中表现突出。

findings.title: 密集监督的必要性
findings.detail: 移除蒸馏损失导致所有基准性能下降，表明密集令牌级监督对于克服奖励稀疏并引导中间推理至关重要。

findings.title: 象限自适应 KL 的有效性
findings.detail: 用固定正向或反向 KL 替代象限自适应 KL 会损害性能，特别是在 TriviaQA（多样拒绝）和 2WikiMultiHopQA（集中整合）上，验证了自适应散度目标的必要性。

contributions: 提出 KbSD，一种利用提示增强教师提供密集令牌级监督以实现知识边界校准的自蒸馏框架。
引入针对四个知识边界象限中异质推理分布的象限自适应 KL 散度目标。
在九个多样化基准上展示了相较强基线持续提升任务准确率和幻觉缓解效果。
通过消融研究验证了密集监督和象限自适应优化的必要性。
发布代码以促进可复现性和后续研究。
limitations: 缺乏对自蒸馏过程计算成本和效率的显式分析。
评估仅限于 Qwen2.5 模型及选定的问答和自主推理基准，未测试对其他架构和任务的泛化能力。
未详细探讨失败模式或推理轨迹的定性分析。
缺乏除经验性 KL 散度调整外的显式机制或因果建模。
open_questions: KbSD 在计算规模上如何扩展，及其在 Qwen2.5 以外更大或不同 LLM 架构上的表现如何？
象限自适应蒸馏框架能否扩展到问答和检索增强生成之外的其他自主任务？
在密集监督下学习的推理轨迹有哪些定性特征，不同象限间有何差异？
KbSD 在真实部署场景中对噪声或对抗性检索证据的鲁棒性如何？

papers.title: IHDec: Divergence-Steered Contrastive Decoding for Securing Multi-Turn Instruction Hierarchies
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) often fail to maintain instruction hierarchies (IH) when processing multi-source inputs with varying role-level priorities, paradoxically adhering to lower-priority directives during conflicts. While existing defenses mitigate this issue, they are largely restricted to single-turn scenarios and require expensive fine-tuning. In this paper, we formalize this failure mode in multi-turn contexts via a Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD) framework, uncovering a pervasive role-influence inversion phenomenon where subordinate inputs override superior roles. To rectify this without training, we propose IHDec (Instruction Hierarchy-steered Decoding). IHDec leverages JSD to automatically detect token-level hierarchy violations and dynamically executes contrastive decoding to suppress misaligned subordinate roles. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that IHDec outperforms training-based baselines in multi-turn conflicts while fully preserving general response quality. Furthermore, IHDec strengthens safety against adversarial prompt injections and exhibits a robust scaling synergy with larger models. The Code is available at https://github.com/nxcolelxu/IHDec.git

summary.takeaway: To rectify this without training, we propose IHDec (Instruction Hierarchy-steered Decoding).

summary.method: In this paper, we formalize this failure mode in multi-turn contexts via a Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD) framework, uncovering a pervasive role-influence inversion phenomenon where subordinate inputs override superior roles.
summary.evidence: Extensive evaluations demonstrate that IHDec outperforms training-based baselines in multi-turn conflicts while fully preserving general response quality.

papers.title: MOPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Capability Integration in LLM Post-Training
papers.abstract: Modern large language models (LLMs) rely on reinforcement learning during post-training to push specific capabilities, yet integrating multiple capabilities into one model remains hard. Existing methods, such as Off-Policy Finetune and Mix-RL, are either inefficient or lose performance. In this work, we propose Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD), a post-training paradigm for combining the capabilities of multiple domain RL teachers: we first run per-domain specialised RL to obtain a set of domain teachers, then distill these teachers into the student on its own rollouts. This eliminates exposure bias and provides a dense optimization signal. On Qwen3-30B-A3B, MOPD outperforms Mix-RL, Cascade RL, Off-Policy Finetune, and Param-Merge baselines, inheriting nearly all of each teacher's capability. MOPD also enables parallel, independent development of domain teachers, removing the cross-domain coupling typical of multi-domain post-training. MOPD has been deployed in the post-training of MiMo-V2-Flash, an industrial-scale frontier model, demonstrating its practical value for capability integration in frontier-scale LLMs.

summary.takeaway: MOPD integrates multiple domain-specific RL teachers into a single LLM via on-policy distillation, achieving superior multi-domain capability without exposure bias or training instability.
summary.problem: Existing multi-capability integration methods for LLM post-training either suffer from inefficiency, exposure bias, instability, or performance degradation.
summary.method: MOPD first trains specialized RL teachers per domain, then distills their policies into a student model on the student's own rollouts using a reverse KL loss with per-prompt teacher dispatch.
summary.evidence: On Qwen3-30B-A3B, MOPD outperforms Mix-RL, Cascade RL, Off-Policy Finetune, and Param-Merge baselines by 5.5 normalized score points, closing 91–95% of the teacher-student performance gap across domains.
summary.limitations: The paper does not provide detailed ablations on the impact of teacher quality variance or the scalability limits of MOPD to more than three domains.
summary.why_for_you: MOPD offers a scalable, stable, and efficient on-policy distillation framework for integrating multiple RL-trained capabilities into a single LLM, directly addressing exposure bias and cross-domain interference.

signals.text: MOPD achieves dense optimization by distilling token-level log-probabilities from multiple frozen domain teachers on the student's own rollout distribution, enabling the student to inherit nearly all capabilities of each teacher.
The method uses a per-token reverse KL loss with two implementations: a policy-gradient form with clipped advantages and a top-k distillation loss that reduces variance and infrastructure overhead.
MOPD eliminates exposure bias by training on the student’s own rollout distribution rather than off-policy teacher rollouts, avoiding the canonical exposure bias seen in Off-Policy Finetune.

deep_dive.overview: The paper addresses the challenge of integrating multiple domain-specific capabilities into a single large language model (LLM) during post-training, a problem where existing methods like Mix-RL, Cascade RL, Off-Policy Finetune, and Param-Merge trade off efficiency, stability, and performance. MOPD proposes a novel on-policy distillation paradigm that first trains specialized RL teachers independently per domain, then distills their policies into a student model by routing each prompt to the corresponding teacher and optimizing a reverse KL loss on the student's own rollouts. This approach provides dense token-level supervision, eliminates exposure bias, and avoids unstable weight-space fusion. Empirical results on Qwen3-30B-A3B across math, instruction following, and software engineering domains demonstrate that MOPD surpasses all baselines by a significant margin, closing most of the gap between the student and specialized teachers. The method also supports parallel teacher development and multi-round student-teacher evolution, making it practical for industrial-scale LLM post-training.

methodology.title: Stage 1: Specialized RL Teacher Training
methodology.detail: Train domain-specific RL teachers independently using specialized pipelines per domain (e.g., verifiable-answer RL for math, agent-style RL for software engineering). Each teacher is frozen after training.

methodology.title: Stage 2: Student Rollout Generation
methodology.detail: The student model generates rollouts by sampling from its own policy distribution, ensuring on-policy data collection that matches the student’s behavior and eliminates exposure bias.

methodology.title: Stage 3: On-Policy Distillation with Per-Prompt Teacher Dispatch
methodology.detail: Each student rollout prompt is routed to the corresponding frozen domain teacher, which provides token-level log-probabilities. The student is optimized via a reverse KL loss between its policy and the dispatched teacher’s policy.

methodology.title: Loss Implementations
methodology.detail: Two loss variants are used: (1) a policy-gradient form with clipped per-token advantages derived from log-probability differences, compatible with PPO/GRPO frameworks; (2) a top-k distillation loss that uses the teacher’s top-k tokens to reduce variance and infrastructure load.

methodology.title: Infrastructure Optimization
methodology.detail: Teacher prefill computations are decoupled from the RL training loop to reduce latency and complexity, enabling efficient per-token log-probability retrieval during distillation.

mechanism.title: On-Policy Distillation via Reverse KL Loss
mechanism.detail: The student policy π_θ is optimized to minimize the reverse KL divergence to the dispatched teacher policy π_φd on the student’s own rollout distribution, expressed as L_rev-KL = E_{x,y~π_θ}[∑_t π_φd(y_t) log(π_θ(y_t))], ensuring dense token-level supervision and stable policy updates.

mechanism.title: Advantage Clipping for Stability
mechanism.detail: The per-token advantage Â_MOPD,t = clip(log π_φd(y_t) - log π_θ(y_t), -A_max, +A_max) is clipped on both sides to prevent large gradient variance and stabilize training within policy-gradient frameworks.

mechanism.title: Top-k Token Distillation Correction
mechanism.detail: The top-k distillation loss includes an additional term π_φd(v) - π_θ(v) beyond the standard reverse KL to correct bias from truncating the teacher’s distribution to top-k tokens, ensuring the loss is minimized when the student matches the teacher on these tokens.

experiments.title: Capability Integration on Qwen3-30B-A3B
experiments.detail: Evaluated on three domains: Math (AIME25, AIME26), Instruction Following (IFBench, IFEval), and Software Engineering (SWE-bench Verified). Baselines include Mix-RL, Cascade RL, Off-Policy Finetune, and Param-Merge. Metrics are per-domain accuracy and a normalized score that scales performance relative to the Stage-1 student and Stage-2 specialist teachers.

experiments.title: Baseline Comparisons
experiments.detail: MOPD outperforms all baselines by 5.5 normalized score points, closing 91–95% of the gap between the Stage-1 student and specialized RL teachers, demonstrating superior multi-domain capability integration.

experiments.title: Loss Variant Ablations
experiments.detail: Both policy-gradient and top-k loss implementations perform comparably, validating the flexibility of MOPD’s distillation approach.

experiments.title: Industrial Deployment
experiments.detail: MOPD was deployed in the post-training of MiMo-V2-Flash, an industrial-scale frontier LLM, where it matched or exceeded teacher performance on most benchmarks, demonstrating practical scalability.

findings.title: Superior Integration Performance
findings.detail: MOPD leads all baselines on Qwen3-30B-A3B with a normalized score improvement of 5.5 points, effectively inheriting nearly all capabilities of each domain teacher.

findings.title: Exposure Bias Elimination
findings.detail: Training on the student’s own rollouts removes exposure bias inherent in off-policy finetuning, contributing to stable and effective capability integration.

findings.title: Stable and Parallelizable Training
findings.detail: Policy-space integration via per-prompt routing avoids unstable weight-space fusion and enables parallel, independent teacher development.

findings.title: Loss Implementation Flexibility
findings.detail: Both policy-gradient and top-k distillation loss forms yield comparable results, offering trade-offs between variance and infrastructure complexity.

findings.title: Multi-Round Student-Teacher Evolution
findings.detail: The pipeline supports iterative improvement cycles between student and teachers, enhancing capability integration over multiple rounds.

contributions: Proposed MOPD, a novel multi-teacher on-policy distillation paradigm for LLM capability integration.
Demonstrated elimination of exposure bias by training on student rollouts with per-prompt teacher dispatch.
Developed two efficient loss implementations (policy-gradient and top-k) for stable distillation.
Empirically validated MOPD’s superiority over four strong baselines on a large-scale LLM across three diverse domains.
Showcased practical deployment of MOPD in industrial-scale LLM post-training with MiMo-V2-Flash.
limitations: Lack of detailed analysis on the impact of teacher quality variance on student performance.
No reported experiments scaling MOPD beyond three domains to assess scalability limits.
Limited discussion on computational cost and latency trade-offs in large-scale deployments.
Absence of theoretical guarantees or formal convergence analysis for the distillation process.
open_questions: How does MOPD scale with an increasing number of domain teachers and more heterogeneous capabilities?
What are the effects of teacher model quality and domain overlap on the final student performance?
Can MOPD be extended to incorporate dynamic teacher updates or online teacher-student co-training?
How does the choice between policy-gradient and top-k loss variants affect convergence speed and final model robustness?

papers.title: EvalSafetyGap: A Hybrid Survey and Conceptual Framework for LLM Evaluation-Safety Failures
papers.abstract: LLM evaluation and AI safety face a shared measurement problem: benchmark scores, reward-model signals, and reported safety metrics can improve while the latent properties they are meant to represent remain difficult to verify. This paper combines a hybrid survey - a systematic search paired with narrative synthesis and separately tracked grey evidence - with a conceptual framework and a structured ten-model audit. The synthesis spans eight evidence streams: benchmark validity, dynamic evaluation, LLM-as-judge reliability, safety evaluation, jailbreak/refusal robustness, reward hacking, mechanistic interpretability, and governance/auditability, covering 2018-2026 evaluation-safety measurement work. We introduce EvalSafetyGap as an organizing hypothesis for comparing evaluation-side and alignment-side proxy failures under optimization pressure, using Goodhart's Law together with two constructs we develop here - an Instability Decomposition and an Alignment Trilemma - as tools for generating testable comparisons. The audit shows how conclusions shift when capability, behavioral safety, and governance are measured separately. In this sample (n = 10), the association between capability and sustained adversarial robustness is statistically indeterminate using the displayed Table 3 inputs (Pearson r = +0.232, p = 0.520), and the apparent open-closed safety gap is modest, driven mainly by governance and disclosure rather than behavioral robustness, and sensitive to how a single borderline model is classified; attempt-budget results are protocol dependent. Because the public evidence uses heterogeneous protocols, the audit is diagnostic rather than rank-generating. The contribution is a shared vocabulary and evidence map to support dynamic evaluation, transparent source reporting, multi-attempt safety measurement, and auditable alignment practice.

summary.takeaway: EvalSafetyGap reveals that LLM evaluation metrics and safety proxies often diverge under optimization pressure, with governance and disclosure driving most observed safety gaps rather than behavioral robustness.
summary.problem: Current LLM evaluation benchmarks and safety metrics improve superficially while failing to reliably measure the latent safety properties they intend to capture.
summary.method: The paper combines a hybrid survey of eight evidence streams with a conceptual framework and a structured ten-model audit to analyze evaluation-safety measurement failures.
summary.evidence: The audit of ten frontier models shows a statistically indeterminate association between capability and adversarial robustness (Pearson r = +0.232, p = 0.520) and highlights protocol-dependent safety gap measurements.
summary.limitations: The audit uses heterogeneous public protocols and a small sample size (n=10), making results diagnostic rather than definitive or rank-generating.
summary.why_for_you: This work provides a shared vocabulary and evidence map critical for developing more reliable, auditable, and dynamic safety evaluation methods for LLMs.

signals.text: The audit finds that the correlation between LLM capability and sustained adversarial robustness is statistically indeterminate (Pearson r = +0.232, p = 0.520), indicating no clear link between improved capability and safety.

EvalSafetyGap introduces two novel constructs—Instability Decomposition and Alignment Trilemma—alongside Goodhart’s Law to systematically compare evaluation-side and alignment-side proxy failures under optimization pressure.

Benchmark saturation leads to metric compression, reducing discriminative power over time, which drives serial benchmark replacement but incurs curation and standardization costs without clear evidence of shortening discriminative lifetimes.

deep_dive.overview: The paper addresses the persistent measurement problem in LLM evaluation and AI safety, where improvements in benchmark scores and safety metrics do not guarantee genuine safety or alignment. It synthesizes eight evidence streams, including benchmark validity, jailbreak robustness, and reward hacking, through a hybrid survey combining systematic review and narrative synthesis. The authors propose EvalSafetyGap as a conceptual framework leveraging Goodhart’s Law, Instability Decomposition, and an Alignment Trilemma to analyze proxy failures in evaluation and alignment under optimization pressure. A structured audit of ten frontier models reveals that capability improvements do not reliably translate to adversarial robustness, and the observed safety gaps are modest and primarily driven by governance and disclosure factors rather than behavioral robustness. The heterogeneous protocols and small sample size limit definitive conclusions, but the work establishes a shared vocabulary and evidence map to guide future dynamic, transparent, and multi-attempt safety evaluations.

methodology.title: Hybrid Survey Design
methodology.detail: Combines systematic literature search with narrative synthesis and tracks grey literature separately to cover eight evidence streams from 2018 to 2026, enabling comprehensive integration of fragmented evaluation-safety research.

methodology.title: Systematic Review Protocol
methodology.detail: Defines review questions, eligibility criteria, information sources, and search strategies with flow accounting and audit trails to ensure reproducibility and transparency in evidence selection and appraisal.

methodology.title: Structured Ten-Model Audit
methodology.detail: Analyzes publicly available data on ten frontier LLMs across capability, behavioral safety, and governance indicators, applying statistical correlation and open-closed gap contrasts to diagnose evaluation-safety relationships.

methodology.title: Conceptual Framework Development
methodology.detail: Introduces EvalSafetyGap hypothesis integrating Goodhart’s Law with Instability Decomposition and Alignment Trilemma constructs to generate testable comparisons between evaluation and alignment proxy failures.

mechanism.title: Goodhart’s Law Application
mechanism.detail: Goodhart’s Law explains how optimization pressure on evaluation proxies leads to divergence from true safety properties, causing proxy failures; the paper identifies four Goodhart mechanisms but does not provide formal equations.

mechanism.title: Instability Decomposition
mechanism.detail: A novel construct decomposing instability in evaluation and alignment proxies under optimization pressure to clarify sources of measurement failure; detailed formalism is not provided in the text.

mechanism.title: Alignment Trilemma
mechanism.detail: A conceptual tool describing trade-offs among capability, behavioral safety, and governance in LLM alignment, highlighting that improvements in one dimension may not generalize to others; no explicit mechanistic model is given.

experiments.title: Ten-Model Frontier Audit
experiments.detail: Evaluates ten state-of-the-art LLMs using seven indicators spanning capability, behavioral safety, and governance; statistical analysis includes Pearson correlation and open-closed safety gap contrasts, revealing protocol-dependent and sample-sensitive results.

experiments.title: Benchmark Saturation Analysis
experiments.detail: Reviews serial benchmark replacement patterns such as MMLU-Pro and Humanity’s Last Exam to assess metric compression and discriminative utility over time, noting the lack of empirical half-life estimates for benchmark effectiveness.

experiments.title: Contamination Detection Survey
experiments.detail: Compares four contamination detection methods (e.g., ConStat, Time Travel) and contamination-resistant benchmark construction approaches to evaluate their capabilities and limitations in preserving construct validity.

findings.title: Indeterminate Capability-Robustness Association
findings.detail: The audit finds no statistically significant correlation between LLM capability and adversarial robustness (Pearson r = +0.232, p = 0.520), suggesting that capability gains do not guarantee improved safety.

findings.title: Governance Drives Safety Gap
findings.detail: The observed open-closed safety gap is modest and primarily attributable to governance and disclosure differences rather than behavioral robustness, with results sensitive to borderline model classification.

findings.title: Benchmark Saturation Reduces Validity
findings.detail: Benchmark saturation leads to metric compression, reducing the benchmarks’ discriminative power and necessitating serial replacements, which incur costs and complicate longitudinal comparisons.

findings.title: LLM-as-Judge Limitations
findings.detail: Meta-evaluation drift and bias taxonomies reveal that LLMs used as judges introduce reliability issues, undermining the validity of safety and capability assessments.

findings.title: Dynamic Evaluation as Partial Solution
findings.detail: Dynamic evaluation methods partially address measurement validity by incorporating multi-attempt and adaptive protocols, but heterogeneity in implementation limits comparability.

contributions: A hybrid survey synthesizing eight evidence streams on LLM evaluation and safety measurement from 2018 to 2026.
The EvalSafetyGap conceptual framework integrating Goodhart’s Law with novel Instability Decomposition and Alignment Trilemma constructs.
A structured ten-model audit demonstrating the diagnostic value of separating capability, behavioral safety, and governance measurements.
A shared vocabulary and evidence map to support dynamic evaluation, transparent reporting, multi-attempt safety measurement, and auditable alignment practice.
limitations: The audit sample size (n=10) is small and uses heterogeneous public protocols, limiting statistical power and generalizability.
No preregistered definitions or standardized protocols for benchmark discriminative utility or safety measurement were applied.
The conceptual constructs (Instability Decomposition, Alignment Trilemma) lack formal mechanistic models or empirical validation.
The review does not estimate benchmark replacement half-lives or quantitatively assess contamination impact across datasets.
open_questions: How can benchmark discriminative utility and replacement half-life be rigorously defined and empirically measured across evolving LLMs?
What are the causal mechanisms underlying the divergence between capability improvements and behavioral safety robustness?
How can dynamic evaluation protocols be standardized to enable reproducible and comparable multi-attempt safety assessments?
Can the Instability Decomposition and Alignment Trilemma constructs be formalized and empirically validated to predict proxy failure modes?

signals.text: 审计发现大型语言模型（LLM）能力与持续对抗鲁棒性之间的相关性在统计上不确定（Pearson r = +0.232，p = 0.520），表明能力提升与安全性之间没有明确联系。
EvalSafetyGap 引入了两个新概念——不稳定性分解（Instability Decomposition）和对齐三难困境（Alignment Trilemma）——以及古德哈特定律（Goodhart’s Law），以系统比较优化压力下评估端和对齐端代理失败。
基准测试饱和导致指标压缩，随着时间推移降低判别能力，推动连续基准替换，但带来策划和标准化成本，且无明确证据表明缩短了判别寿命。

zh-CN.overview: 本文针对大型语言模型（LLM）评估和人工智能安全中的持续测量问题展开，指出基准分数和安全指标的提升并不保证真正的安全或对齐。通过结合系统综述与叙述综合的混合调查，综合了包括基准有效性、越狱鲁棒性和奖励黑客等八条证据线。作者提出 EvalSafetyGap 作为概念框架，利用古德哈特定律、不稳定性分解和对齐三难困境分析优化压力下评估与对齐代理失败。对十个前沿模型的结构化审计显示，能力提升未必可靠地转化为对抗鲁棒性，观察到的安全差距较小，主要由治理和披露因素驱动，而非行为鲁棒性。异质协议和样本量小限制了确定性结论，但该工作建立了共享词汇和证据地图，指导未来动态、透明和多次尝试的安全评估。

methodology.title: 混合调查设计
methodology.detail: 结合系统文献检索与叙述综合，单独追踪灰色文献，覆盖2018年至2026年的八条证据线，实现对分散评估-安全研究的全面整合。

methodology.title: 结构化十模型审计
methodology.detail: 分析十个前沿大型语言模型的公开数据，涵盖能力、行为安全和治理指标，应用统计相关性和开放-封闭差距对比，诊断评估-安全关系。

methodology.title: 概念框架开发
methodology.detail: 提出 EvalSafetyGap 假说，整合古德哈特定律与不稳定性分解及对齐三难困境构建，生成评估与对齐代理失败的可检验比较。

mechanism.title: 古德哈特定律应用
mechanism.detail: 古德哈特定律解释了优化压力如何导致评估代理与真实安全属性偏离，产生代理失败；本文识别了四种古德哈特机制，但未提供形式化方程。

mechanism.title: 不稳定性分解
mechanism.detail: 一种新颖构建，分解优化压力下评估与对齐代理的不稳定性，澄清测量失败来源；文本中未提供详细形式化描述。

mechanism.title: 对齐三难困境
mechanism.detail: 描述大型语言模型对齐中能力、行为安全和治理三者权衡的概念工具，强调一维度改进不一定推广至其他维度；未给出明确机制模型。

experiments.title: 十模型前沿审计
experiments.detail: 使用涵盖能力、行为安全和治理的七个指标评估十个最先进大型语言模型；统计分析包括 Pearson 相关和开放-封闭安全差距对比，结果依赖协议且对样本敏感。

papers.title: Reward-Free Code Alignment from Pretrained or Fine-Tuned LLM: Unpacking the Trade-offs for Code Generation
papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) alignment trains an LLM using preference data to produce outputs that better meet established quality standards. While LLM alignment techniques are studied for non-coding tasks, we know little about their usefulness for coding tasks. It is unclear whether LLM code alignment could support both functional requirements (producing executable, correct code) and non-functional requirements (code readability, style, maintainability). It is also unknown whether alignment for a code LLM should begin with base pretrained version or the finetuned (i.e., instruction-tuned) version of the LLM. In this paper, we offer insights on the above two research questions by conducting an empirical study. We studied five state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs using two widely used LLM alignment techniques: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and BoNBoN. For each training record, we created a preference pair as accepted and rejected instances by using the SelfCodeAlign pipeline. DPO and BoNBoN are reward-free models, i.e., they eliminate the need for multiple reward scores for output preferences. We tuned each LLM using the two alignment techniques in two settings: pretrained and finetuned versions of an LLM. We evaluated functional requirements using four SOTA benchmarks (HumanEval+, MBPP+, EvalPerf, EvoEval) and non-functional requirements using the CODAL benchmark, which evaluates code quality across five dimensions derived from software engineering practices. We find that pretrained-to-aligned pathways achieve larger improvements in the aligned variant over its pretrained variant. But the pretrained variant is generally less accurate than its finetuned variant. However, finetuned- to-aligned offers smaller performance improvements or, in some cases, degradation in the aligned variant than its finetuned variant.

papers.title: SrDetection: A Self-Referential Framework for Data Leakage Detection in Code Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Evaluating code large language models (Code LLMs) requires reliable detection of data leakage, where benchmark performance is artificially inflated by exposure to benchmark data during pre-training. Existing approaches either assume access to proprietary training corpora, rely on brittle heuristics such as timestamp filtering, or use external reference sets with manually tuned, non-generalizable thresholds. To address these limitations, we introduce \textbf{SrDetection}, a unified \textbf{s}elf-\textbf{r}eferential leakage detection framework for both gray-box (access to model logits) and black-box (access to model outputs) settings. SrDetection generates semantically equivalent variants of a benchmark sample and detects leakage by contrasting the model's behavior on the original versus its variants, flagging cases where the original is disproportionately easier for the model. We further design a controlled leakage detection testbed and evaluate SrDetection in this environment. Across different models and training stages, SrDetection improves average F1 by 21.52 points in the gray-box setting and 14.46 points in the black-box setting over strong baselines, demonstrating robust, threshold-independent leakage detection. Finally, a gray-box study of 15 widely used Code LLMs on four popular benchmarks reveals benchmark-specific leakage patterns beyond prior overlap-based analyses\footnote{\footnotesize Source code and data are available at https://github.com/SMinL/SrDetectionCode

papers.title: Budgeted Act-or-Defer Multi-Agent LLM Deliberation with Local Reliability Bounds
papers.abstract: Multi-agent deliberation among LLMs can improve reasoning, but deployment requires deciding when the current answer is reliable enough to act on and when it should be escalated to human review. We formulate this as budgeted act-or-defer decision making. At each round, the system maps the debate prefix to a low-dimensional state, computes a $k$-nearest-neighbor lower confidence bound on state-conditional correctness using calibration data, and acts only when the bound exceeds a user-specified reliability threshold. The certificate controls wrong actions through the decomposition $β= δ+ α+ \varepsilon_{\mathrm{act}}$, separating calibration failure, residual action risk, and representation gap. The guarantee is conditional, not distribution-free: it relies on a valid local bias envelope and an action-region representation-gap bound, and each assumption is paired with falsification-style diagnostics. Because the same absolute wrong-action budget has different meanings across tasks of different difficulty, we set budgets relative to each task's final-round error using training data only, and evaluate safety by normalized budget usage $\mathrm{WA}/β$. On six benchmarks against nine baselines, the method uses 9--12% of the pre-declared budget on activated datasets, reaching up to 84% automation and 96% acted-on accuracy; on stress-test datasets, it defers rather than forcing unreliable automation. Rather than relying on per-task post-hoc threshold search, the method prospectively converts a user-declared wrong-action budget into an auditable act-or-defer operating point before deployment, under explicitly stated assumptions.

papers.title: The Heterogeneous Safety Impacts of Benign Multilingual Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning a large language model is a ubiquitous method for enhancing its capability on a specific downstream task. However, prior work has shown that this increase in capability comes with a cost: it can increase a model's tendency to respond to unsafe adversarial prompts, even when fine-tuning with non-adversarial data. We present the first comprehensive empirical study of this phenomenon in multilingual settings by fine-tuning Llama-3.2, Qwen3, and Gemma-3 models using benign data translated across nine languages. We find that safety outcomes are highly sensitive to both the choice of fine-tuning language and the evaluation language, with adversarial compliance rates increasing four-fold in some settings. Multilingual safety drift is decoupled from general capability metrics, and occurs heterogeneously across languages and models. Fine-tuning in non-English languages often induces smaller internal representational drifts than English, but these shifts lead models to default to either exaggerated compliance or refusal. As such, assessing fine-tuning impacts solely in English provides inadequate assurance for deployment. To facilitate further research into these cross-lingual safety blind spots, we release the Multilingual-Benign-Tune dataset and the SORRY-Bench-Multilingual evaluation suite.

papers.title: Robust Harmful Features Under Jailbreak Attacks: Mechanistic Evidence from Attention Head Specialization in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Jailbreak attacks bypass LLM safety alignment, yet their mechanisms remain poorly understood. We provide evidence that attacks do not comprehensively eliminate safety features, but instead selectively suppress specific attention heads. We identify two functionally differentiated types: Adversarially Compromised Heads (ACHs) concentrated in early layers, which are suppressed under attacks, and Safety-Aligned Heads (SAHs) in mid-layers, which maintain robust activations even when attacks succeed. Ablation studies support the causal role of ACHs and the contribution of SAHs to robust activations: suppressing a small number of ACHs is sufficient to induce jailbreak-like behavior on normally refused inputs, while removing SAHs substantially weakens mid-layer safety activations. Token-level attribution further shows that ACH suppression is driven specifically by attack-template tokens, providing a mechanistic account of why attacks can bypass refusal decisions through ACH suppression while leaving internal safety signals sustained by SAHs -- a phenomenon we term Robust Harmful Features. To validate the practical significance of this robustness, we show that simply reading these persistent activations -- without any training -- yields competitive aggregate detection performance with strong adversarial robustness.

papers.title: Low-Agreeableness Persona Conditioning for Safe LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Recent work has shown that fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) for social warmth degrades factual reliability and increases sycophancy. We investigate a related but distinct failure mode: warmth fine-tuning also weakens adversarial safety, making models more susceptible to jailbreaks and harmful output generation. We examine whether this reflects an inherent consequence of empathetic adaptation or an artifact of data construction. To address this, we introduce a persona-driven rewriting pipeline that conditions user turns on low agreeableness and pairs this with warm, de-escalating assistant responses. Across three experiments on four models, our approach reduces jailbreak susceptibility and harmful output rates relative to generic warmth fine-tuning baselines, while preserving conversational warmth. Representational probing provides suggestive evidence that this conditioning reduces the geometric alignment between warmth and compliance directions in latent space. These results show that safer empathetic fine-tuning is achievable through data design alone, without safety labels, harm detectors, or changes to the training objective.

papers.title: ToolPrivacyBench: Benchmarking Purpose-Bound Privacy in Tool-Using LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have increasingly moved from standalone text generation systems to agents that invoke external tools, access environments, and execute multi-step tasks. However, conventional function-calling benchmarks mainly evaluate task completion and API correctness, while privacy evaluation benchmarks typically focus on final responses or privacy judgments. Neither perspective captures purpose-bound information flow across an executed multi-tool trajectory. Motivated by this limitation in current agent evaluation, ToolPrivacyBench audits whether task-private atoms are routed only to authorized tools and downstream sinks, thereby evaluating both task completion and privacy over-disclosure during tool use. The benchmark contains 2,150 cases, including 1,150 fully synthetic privacy-sensitive business workflows and 1,000 cases adapted from existing multi-tool and function-calling benchmarks. Each case is represented by a policy knowledge base. After an agent executes against mock business backends, the evaluator compares recorded tool arguments and backend audit logs with this policy knowledge base. The evaluation covers nine widely used agents to characterize purpose-bound privacy over-disclosure. The results show that successful tool execution does not imply appropriate privacy disclosure: an agent may complete a task while transmitting unnecessary private information through intermediate tool calls. ToolPrivacyBench therefore formalizes a need-to-know disclosure boundary, under which each tool should receive only the information necessary for its stated purpose, and uses trajectory-level auditing to identify privacy over-disclosure in multi-tool workflows.

summary.method: ToolPrivacyBench audits information flow using a policy knowledge base to ensure only necessary data is shared with tools.
summary.evidence: The benchmark includes 2,150 cases and evaluates nine widely used agents, revealing that task completion does not guarantee appropriate privacy disclosure.
summary.limitations: The study does not provide evidence on the effectiveness of privacy measures in real-world applications.

papers.title: Paved with True Intents: Intent-Aware Training Improves LLM Safety Classification Across Training Regimes
papers.abstract: We argue that safety classifiers should model user intent as an explicit signal between the prompt and the final label. To study this, we introduce AIMS, a human-annotated dataset of 1,724 difficult safety prompts, each paired with an intent description and harm label. We use AIMS to evaluate intent-aware training across supervised fine-tuning, preference learning, reasoning distillation, and reinforcement learning. Despite its size, AIMS enables competitive safety classifiers across training regimes: DPO from model-generated intent errors improves over SFT, and intent-conditioned distillation outperforms reasoning-only distillation in most teacher-student pairs. Most notably, directly rewarding intent faithfulness with GRPO yields the strongest average performance across five external safety benchmarks, while our intent-aware models form the inference latency-F1 Pareto frontier. These results show that faithful intent modeling is a compact, high-quality supervision signal for more robust safety classifiers.

papers.title: Yuvion LLM: An Adversarially-Aware Large Language Model for Content And AI Safety
papers.abstract: As large language models are increasingly deployed in real-world systems, safety failures can still lead to harmful outputs and dangerous misuse. We argue that the essence of safety is adversarial: many failures arise not from natural inputs alone, but from strategic attempts to evade model policies and safeguards. However, existing general-purpose model development largely overlook this adversarial nature, and often remain insufficient for realistic safety scenarios involving planning, tool use, and multi-step reasoning, causing measured safety performance to overestimate real deployment robustness. To address this gap, we present Yuvion LLM, a large language model built for adversarially robust content safety and broader AI safety. Yuvion LLM treats adversarial robustness and agentic capability as first-class objectives. Its pipeline combines adversarially aware data construction, knowledge-enhanced continued pretraining, and policy-grounded multi-task safety post-training, including risk-aware supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning-based policy optimization, together with safety-aware agentic reinforcement learning for tool use and multi-step reasoning in complex safety scenarios. We further introduce the Yuvion LLM RiskEval (YLRE), a collection of 93 benchmarks across four evaluation categories, covering diverse open and internal evaluations with a focus on safety, adversarial robustness, and real-world capability requirements. Across these evaluations, Yuvion LLM demonstrates clear advantages on safety-focused benchmarks and particularly strong robustness under adversarial conditions, while maintaining solid overall capability. Notably, Yuvion-8B outperforms most state-of-the-art baselines, including substantially larger models such as GPT-5.4 and Qwen3-MAX, on several safety tasks.

summary.takeaway: Yuvion LLM is designed specifically for adversarial robustness and AI safety, integrating multiple advanced training techniques.
summary.problem: Existing large language models often fail to adequately address adversarial threats, leading to safety vulnerabilities in real-world applications.
summary.method: The authors develop Yuvion LLM using adversarially aware data construction, knowledge-enhanced continued pretraining, and multi-task safety post-training.

papers.title: From Signals to Transfer: A Factorised Study of Probe-Based Uncertainty Estimation in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Probe-based uncertainty estimation (UE) has emerged as a prominent approach to detect hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs) by learning uncertainty from internal model signals. Yet, recent methods vary simultaneously across feature design, training data construction, and evaluation setting, obscuring what actually drives performance. To address this issue, we propose a factorised study of probe-based UE under matched conditions. Our results show that raw hidden states and attention features are difficult to outperform in-domain. However, under distribution shift, structured and compressed features are more robust, suggesting that in-domain performance alone is insufficient to measure progress. Furthermore, prompting and label construction significantly affect probe behaviour. Building on these best-practice findings, we train benchmark-based pretrained probes that transfer reasonably well to open-ended factual generation, providing a stable off-the-shelf baseline. Our work encourages more deployment-oriented evaluation of probe-based uncertainty estimators. The code repository is available at https://github.com/ponhvoan/ProbeUE.

papers.title: NebulaExp-8B: An Empirical Post-Training Pipeline via Full-Scale Ablation Research
papers.abstract: Post-training alignment determines the reasoning and human preference following capabilities of large language models, yet most existing works withhold detailed data construction, filtering rules and training recipes, which hinders community reproducibility and lightweight model optimization. This work presents NebulaExp, a fully transparent, ablation-driven post-training pipeline built on Qwen3-8B-base, covering two orthogonal model branches: general instruct model and complex reasoning-specialized model. We curate a raw corpus of 3.84M multi-source SFT samples and a 200K verifiable RL candidate pool, and design an end-to-end data processing stack including response distillation, multi-dimensional cross-verification filtering, fine-grained difficulty grading, task classification and diversity-aware sampling. For the Instruct branch, our three-stage optimized supervised fine-tuning approach NebulaExp-Ins-SFT improves the average benchmark score from the 55.01 baseline of Qwen3-8B-nothink to 60.99. GRPO reinforcement learning then further elevates the average score to 61.85. For the Reasoning branch, medium-difficulty GRPO RL improves average reasoning score from 73.88 to 75.17. To address RL's dependency on task verifiers, we systematically investigate single-teacher and multi-teacher OPD (MOPD): utilizing merely 4K instruction-following samples and outperforms RL baseline by 3.26 points on IFEval with +4.43 average overall gain; MOPD fuses four domain-specialist teachers with merely 10K samples, lifting average performance by 4.18 over the base model. This report provides a fully reproducible empirical post-training recipe for 8B-scale LLMs, and comprehensively dissects the capability trade-offs among instruction adherence, mathematical reasoning, code generation and general knowledge.

papers.title: Reasoning Quality Emerges Early: Data Curation for Reasoning Models
papers.abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on a small, high-quality set of long reasoning traces is an effective approach for eliciting strong reasoning capabilities in Large Language Models (LLMs). However, existing methods for curating high-quality SFT data rely heavily on strong reasoning models to filter examples based on diversity and difficulty, making the curation process costly while often yielding suboptimal data quality. In this work, we show that diverse and challenging reasoning examples can be identified using only the initial reasoning tokens. Specifically, we demonstrate that difficult problems can be reliably detected based on the loss of the first 100 reasoning tokens evaluated at a randomly perturbed checkpoint of the pretrained model. We further show that examples exhibiting similar loss patterns over their first 1k reasoning tokens across a small number of perturbed checkpoints extrapolating along the fine-tuning trajectory provably induce similar gradients. We validate our approach through extensive experiments on fine-tuning Qwen2.5-7B and Llama3.1-8B models on the M23K medical reasoning and OpenThoughts-Math datasets. Our method outperforms existing baselines by up to 1.7% while being 91% more token efficient.

summary.takeaway: The study presents a novel method for identifying high-quality reasoning examples using only initial reasoning tokens, improving data curation for LLMs.

papers.title: At the Edge of Understanding: Sparse Autoencoders Trace The Limits of Transformer Generalization
papers.abstract: Pre-trained transformers have demonstrated remarkable generalization abilities, at times extending beyond the scope of their training data. Yet, real-world deployments often face unexpected or adversarial data that diverges from training data distributions. Without explicit mechanisms for handling such shifts, model reliability and safety degrade, urging more disciplined study of out-of-distribution (OOD) settings for transformers. By systematic experiments, we present a mechanistic framework for delineating the precise contours of transformer model robustness. We find that OOD inputs, including subtle typos and jailbreak prompts, drive language models to operate on an increased number of fallacious concepts in their internals. We leverage this device to quantify and understand the degree of distributional shift in prompts, enabling a mechanistically grounded fine-tuning strategy to robustify LLMs. Expanding the very notion of OOD from input data to a model's private computational processes, a new transformer diagnostic at inference time is a critical step toward making AI systems safe for deployment across science, business, and government.

papers.title: GEOALIGN: Geometric Rollout Curation for Robust LLM Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Online reinforcement learning is widely used to align large language models (LLMs) with reward signals, yet training can be unstable under noisy or misspecified rewards. We identify a failure mode we call directional inconsistency: within a batch, a small set of high-reward rollouts induces representation-space preference directions that sharply disagree with the batch majority, resulting in high-variance and destabilizing updates. We propose geoalign, a lightweight plug-in for rollout curation in iterative policy optimization. Geoalign (i) forms within-prompt preference pairs, (ii) learns an online projector on per-rollout hidden states to concentrate reward-ordered displacement directions, and (iii) detects directionally inconsistent rollouts via their angular deviation from a batch consensus prototype and rectifies them with within-prompt stable alternatives. Geoalign is forward-pass only and adds negligible overhead. Across dialogue alignment with a learned reward model and mathematical reasoning with binary verified rewards, Geoalign improves final performance and reduces training oscillation, outperforming PF-PPO, PAR, PODS, and Seed-GRPO. These results suggest latent directional consensus as an effective reliability signal for online LLM RL.

papers.title: Agents That Know Too Much: A Data-Centric Survey of Privacy in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large language model agents increasingly query databases, search document collections, call external APIs, remember past interactions, and act on a user's behalf. As they move from answering questions to operating over sensitive data, privacy becomes harder to enforce. An agent touches many data sources, runs multi-step workflows, keeps state across sessions, and acts with delegated permissions. Sensitive information can therefore leak not only through its final answer but through the queries it issues, the intermediate results it handles, the memory it writes, and the messages it exchanges with other agents. We survey the privacy of LLM agents from a data-centric view, organizing the field around the data an agent touches rather than by attack type, and we use data agent as shorthand for an LLM agent that works with data. Research on these risks is active but scattered across retrieval-augmented generation, text-to-SQL interfaces, agent memory, prompt injection, access control, and contextual privacy. This survey brings that work together: we taxonomize the data sources an agent touches, the privacy risks each source creates, and the governance mechanisms that address them; we map the benchmarks used to measure these risks and identify what is missing; and we set out the open problems. Two findings recur: among governance mechanisms only information-flow control covers both compositional and cross-session inference leakage, the two least-protected risks; and no benchmark drives an agent across its data surfaces under one privacy policy, the instrument the field most lacks. Our goal is a reference that situates the scattered literature and gives future work a common framing.

summary.takeaway: The survey organizes and synthesizes privacy risks associated with LLM agents from a data-centric perspective, highlighting gaps in governance mechanisms and benchmarks.
summary.problem: As LLM agents increasingly handle sensitive data, enforcing privacy becomes more complex due to their interactions with multiple data sources.
summary.method: The authors taxonomize data sources, privacy risks, governance mechanisms, and benchmarks related to LLM agents, while identifying open problems in the field.

summary.limitations: The authors note that no benchmark currently evaluates an agent's data interactions under a unified privacy policy.
